text: By the rivers of Babylon (confusion by mixing) we sat and wept when we remembered Zion.
There on the willows (poplars) we hung our harps,
for there our captors requested a song; our tormentors demanded songs of joy: “Sing us a song of Zion.”
How can we sing a song of the LORD {YHWH} in a foreign land?
If I forget you, O Jerusalem (city of peace), may my right hand cease to function.
May my tongue cling to the roof of my mouth if I do not remember you, if I do not exalt Jerusalem (city of peace) as my greatest joy!
Remember, O LORD {YHWH}, the sons of Edom (red) on the day Jerusalem fell (city of peace): “Destroy it,” they said, “tear it down to its foundations!”
O Daughter of Babylon (confusion by mixing), doomed to destruction, blessed is he who repays you as you have done to us.
Blessed is he who seizes your infants and dashes them against the rocks.
